This appeal is preferred by the appellants/petitioners challenging the judgment and award passed by the Court of the III Addl.Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.897/2019 dated 18.09.2021, on the ground of inadequate and meager compensation.

entities.text: III Addl.Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are;
The petitioners are the mother and sister of deceased Shivakumar S/o Shankarappa.

That on 15.04.2019 while Shivakumar was returning in Car bearing Reg.No.KA-32/N- 2145 from Kamalapur to Kalaburagi after attending his personal work, when he came near Navadagi Bridge on Kalaburagi-Humnabad National Highway Main Road No.218 within the limits of Mahagaon Police Station at that time the driver of Toofan Trax bearing Reg.No.KA-28/M-6040 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner with high speed without following traffic rules, came extremely towards wrong side and dashed the car of Shivakumar.
As a result of which, Shvakumar sustained fatal injuries to the vital parts of the body and died on the spot.
4. It is stated that the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years.
He was studying B.Sc.VI Semester at Reshmi College, Kalaburagi and was conducting tutorial classes by which he was earning monthly income of `30,000/-.
Apart from that he was doing agriculture work and earning Rs.3,00,000/- per annum.

The deceased was the only earning member of the family, who Mallamma And Anr vs Maibubsab And Anr on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4889276/
2 used to look after his mother-first petitioner herein and his sister-2nd petitioner for her educational and marriage prospects.

sentences.text: In view of sudden and untimely death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their sole bread earner, love and affection and also have suffered mentally and financially.

Hence,
they filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. On service of notice, respondent No.1 filed objection statement denying the averments made in the petition and stated that accident took place because of negligent driving by the deceased.
Respondent No.2 filed detailed statement of objections denying inter alia age, avocation and income including the death of deceased as alleged in the claim petition.

It is further pleaded that the driver of offending Toofan Trax bearing Reg.No.KA-28/M- 6040 was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and hence on these grounds, sought for dismissal of claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the mother of deceased was examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P38.
Respondents have not examined any of the witnesses but with consent got marked Ex.R1 the insurance policy of the Toofan Trax.

7. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary, the Tribunal fastened liability on the respondents and awarded total compensation of `14,86,000/- with 6% interest per annum and directed the respondent No.2/Insurance Company to deposit the compensation.

8. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is erroneous, contrary to the material evidence placed on record and the documents presented by the petitioners.
On this basis, they seek enhancement of compensation and consequently allow the appeal.

9. Per contra, learned counsel Smt.Preethi Patil, Adv., appearing on behalf of respondent No.2 vehemently contends that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is in consonance with the material evidence placed on record and the same in fact is on the higher side.

Learned counsel further contends that the award of compensation on the other heads are suitably calculated and rightly awarded, which does not call for interference and on the basis of these submissions, he seeks to dismiss the appeal filed by the petitioners.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants/petitioners and learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are:
i) Whether the petitioners are entitled to enhancement of compensation ?
ii) What order"
11.

On a careful perusal of entire material on record and having gone through the impugned judgment and award including the exhibits marked in the case on hand, it Mallamma And Anr vs Maibubsab And Anr on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4889276/
3 is apparently seen that the petitioners would be entitled for enhancement of compensation for the reason stated herein below :-
(a) It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 15.04.2019 between tractor and car leading to the death of deceased-Shivakumar S/o.Shankarappa.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These aspects have been proved by way of production of Ex.P1 to P38.
Admittedly, there is no challenge made to the initiation of criminal prosecution and laying of charge-sheet.
The Insurance Company has not filed any appeal against the judgment and award.

Under the circumstances, there is no requirement for this Court to delve into the occurrence of accident, involvement of the vehicles and so also the death having occurred due to the road traffic accident.
(b) Now, the question that is to be decided by this Court is whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager and whether calls for interference by this Court.

It is relevant to quote the decision in Syed Basheer Ahmed vs. Mohammed Zameer1 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court noticed that Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act enjoins the claims Tribunal to make an award determining "the amount of compensation which appears to be just".

entities.text: Syed Basheer Ahmed vs. Mohammed Zameer1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, the objective factors,
which may constitute the basis of compensation appearing as just, have not been indicated in the Act.

Thus, the expression "which appears to be just"
vests wide discretion in the Claims Tribunal in the matter of determination of compensation.

Nevertheless, the wide amplitude of such power does not empower the Tribunal to determine the compensation arbitrarily or to ignore settled principles relating to the determination of the compensation.

Similarly, although the Act is a beneficial legislation, it can neither be allowed to be used as a source of profit nor as a windfall to the persons affected nor should it be punitive to (2009) 2 SCC 225 the persons liable to pay compensation.

The determination of the compensation must be based on certain data, establishing reasonable nexus between the loss incurred by the dependents of the deceased and the compensation to be awarded to them.
In a nutshell, the amount of compensation determined to be payable to the petitioners has to be fair and reasonable by accepted legal standards.

(c) The determination of the quantum must answer what "contemporary society would deem to be a fair sum such as would allow the wrong doer to hold up his head among his neighbours and say with their approval that he has done the fair thing".
The amount awarded must not be niggardly since the "law values life and limb in a free Society in generous case".
At the same time, misplaced sympathy, generosity and benevolence cannot be the guiding factor for determining compensation.

The object of providing compensation is to please the petitioners to the extent possible, in almost the same financial position as they were in before the accident and not to make a fortune out of misfortune that has befallen them.

sentences.text: (d) On the basis of the material evidence placed before this Court, it is seen that the deceased was aged about 22 years studying and doing agricultural work and earning `30,000/- per month.
In the absence of relevant documents to show the income, the Tribunal has rightly taken the monthly income of the deceased at `13,250/-.
The deceased being aged 22 years is entitled to 40% increase towards future prospects in addition to the notional income chart value for assessment of income.

In view of the fact that the deceased was aged 22 years, the appropriate multiplier would be '18'
which is rightly taken by the Tribunal.
Same does not call for interference.

(e) Evidently, the deceased Shivakumar was studying apart from doing agricultural work and conducting tutorial classes, addition of 40% towards loss of future prospects to be added as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2, which would be `18,550/- (`13,250/- + 5,300 (40%)).
(f) As the deceased was bachelor, 50% of his income is to be deducted towards his personal expenses as contemplated in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and another3, which would be `9,275/- (50% of `18,550).

The deceased was aged 22 years at the time of accident and as per the decision in the case of Sarala Varma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another4, the proper multiplier applicable is `18'.

sentences.text: Thus, the total loss of dependency would be `20,03,400/- (Rs.1,11,300 x18).
(g) Petitioner No.2 being the mother of the deceased has lost her beloved son being bread earner.

Since there are two dependants mother and sister of the deceased, they are entitled to `40,000/- towards consortium per head as (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121 (2009 ACJ 1298) contemplated in the case of Pranay Sethi stated supra, which has been subsequently followed in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., v. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others5.

(h) Towards 'loss of estate' and towards 'transportation of dead body & funeral expenses', petitioners would be entitled to `15,000/- each i.e., a sum of `30,000/-
requires to be awarded and it is accordingly awarded.
Accordingly, under conventional head `1,10,000/- (loss of consortium `80,000/- + loss of estate `15,000/- + Towards transportation of dead body & funeral expenses `15,000/-) is awarded.
(i) As per the decision in Pranay Sethi, stated supra, 10% on the conventional head for each block period requires to be awarded, which in the present case would be `11,000/- for one block period.

Thus the AIR 2020 SC 3076 appellant/petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation as under:

In view of our discussion, with regard to the actionable claim and the compensation to be awarded to the petitioner, the appeal filed by the petitioner deserves to be allowed in-part.

Resultantly, we pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in-part.
The Judgment and Award dated 18.09.2021 passed in MVC No.897/2019 by the III Addl.Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T, Kalaburagi, is modified.
The appellants-petitioners are held entitled for enhanced compensation of `6,39,000/- together with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

The respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the said enhanced compensation before the III Addl.Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T, Kalaburagi within four weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
